segments.text: Welcome to today's Robot Report, your daily dose of robotics news.
I'm your host, and we're diving into the latest developments that are shaping the future of automation.
Robots are learning on the job, humans are taking control, and open-source just got a boost - let's dive in!
From The Robot Report, "Reimagine Robotics emerges from stealth with robots that ‘learn on the job’.
Reimagine Robotics has developed a system allowing robots to learn tasks through human instruction, effectively bypassing specialist programmers for task changes.
This approach relies on people identifying bottlenecks, teaching robots, and correcting them until they become useful.

The startup claims its technology enables workers to show the robot what to do, watch it attempt the task, and correct it immediately, significantly reducing the need for traditional programming methods.

Reimagine Robotics has already deployed its robots in advanced manufacturing and electronics disassembly facilities, achieving a notable reduction in prototype testing time from a day to just 10 minutes.
From The Robot Report, "Google DeepMind says Gemini Robotics 2 enables full body control,"

Google DeepMind has announced that its Gemini Robotics 2 model can now enable full-body control of humanoid robots like Apptronik's Apollo 2, allowing them to reason through every movement and unlock a broad range of tasks.

This breakthrough is made possible by the model's ability to manage complex tasks that require multiple steps over an extended period, self-correct if a step fails, and generalize to novel situations and goals.
Gemini Robotics ER 2 is now available on Google AI Studio and in private preview on the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, while Gemini Robotics On-Device 2 targets applications with low connectivity.
The model can adapt to new robot embodiments with just a few hours of adaptation time, marking a significant advancement in humanoid robotics control.
This development has the potential to significantly impact various industries that rely on intelligent robots for tasks such as healthcare and manufacturing.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: ROS 2 Realtime Support Package,"
a new package called ros2_realtime_support has been developed to provide real-time functionality for ROS 2 without modifying existing packages.
This package is designed to be used with rclcpp and enables users to enable real-time support by adding a configuration file, changing the main routine in source files, and updating certain classes.
The development of this package is ongoing, with plans to improve mutexes and condition variables on RTOS in future work.
"And that's a wrap for another day of robotic revelations!
Thanks for joining me, folks - may the wires be ever in your favor!
Until tomorrow, when we'll gear up again, farewell for now."
